articles.headline: Google's head of energy and power on how AI data centers can help improve the grid
articles.summary: AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting pressure on America’s power grid. Google says its planned 780MW data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will pay for 1,900MW of renewable grid upgrades to the area while protecting local ratepayers. CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos interviews Google's global head of energy and power, Amanda Peterson Corio, to learn more.

articles.headline: The race to power AI data centers is reshaping America's electric grid

Google says its planned 780MW data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will support 1,900 megawatts of renewable energy and ways to protect local ratepayers. CNBC examines if projects like this can help upgrade the grid without shifting costs to residents.
